id: guest facing reservation and property systems
name: Guest-facing reservation and property systems
description: Core operational software that, if encrypted or disrupted, halts check-in/out, room assignment, and bookings, causing immediate revenue and reputational loss.

id: payment and point of sale pos infrastructure
name: Payment and point-of-sale (POS) infrastructure
description: High-volume, PCI-DSS-regulated transaction systems across hotels, restaurants, casinos, and venues that are prime ransomware/extortion targets due to payment card data and operational criticality.

id: guest and member personal data pii
name: Guest and member personal data (PII)
description: Large repositories of sensitive personal and financial data accumulated through loyalty programs, bookings, and identity verification, making this sector attractive for double-extortion data leaks.

id: casino and gaming specific systems
name: Casino- and gaming-specific systems
description: Specialized OT/IT-blended systems unique to the gaming vertical within this sector, where downtime directly halts revenue-generating floor operations.

id: third party and supply chain exposure
name: Third-party and supply-chain exposure
description: Extensive outsourcing and franchise/partner relationships common to hospitality, food service, and entertainment create indirect exposure when a vendor, franchisee, or partner is compromised.

id: building iot and physical operations technology
name: Building, IoT, and physical-operations technology
description: Smart-building and physical-plant systems increasingly networked to corporate IT, creating an OT-adjacent attack surface distinct to physically large hospitality/entertainment venues.

id: corporate financial and employee systems
name: Corporate, financial, and employee systems
description: Back-office systems common to any large multi-site employer, holding data attractive for extortion beyond guest-facing systems.

id: production and operational technology systems
name: Production & Operational Technology Systems
description: The plant-floor and field systems whose disruption stops physical output and threatens food safety and animal welfare.

id: enterprise it erp and ordering logistics platforms
name: Enterprise IT, ERP & Ordering/Logistics Platforms
description: The business systems that, when encrypted, halt ordering, invoicing, dispatch and payment even when the physical plant is intact.

id: sensitive data assets
name: Sensitive Data Assets
description: Data types whose theft drives extortion, regulatory penalties, and national-security concern.

id: third party and supply chain dependencies
name: Third-Party & Supply-Chain Dependencies
description: Transportation/warehousing firms rely heavily on shared vendor platforms and interconnected partner networks, concentrating risk in a small number of upstream providers.

id: physical goods livestock and continuity assets
name: Physical Goods, Livestock & Continuity Assets
description: Sector-unique tangible exposures that convert cyber downtime into direct physical loss.

id: project and design data
name: Project and Design Data
description: The core intellectual property of a construction or engineering firm, of high value both for extortion leverage and to competitors.

id: bid contract and financial data
name: Bid, Contract and Financial Data
description: Commercially sensitive project economics and the financial systems that manage them - a favored ransomware and extortion target.

id: employee and workforce pii
name: Employee and Workforce PII
description: Personal data held on large, often multi-employer workforces.

id: field and jobsite systems
name: Field and Jobsite Systems
description: Technology deployed at or connecting to active construction sites, often with weaker security posture than corporate headquarters.

id: building management and facilities systems
name: Building Management and Facilities Systems
description: Operational technology exposure that persists beyond project completion, for firms with ongoing facilities-management, warranty or operations contracts.

id: third party and subcontractor networks
name: Third-Party and Subcontractor Networks
description: External parties and shared infrastructure that extend a construction firm's attack surface beyond its own perimeter.

id: client and government owner data
name: Client and Government-Owner Data
description: Sensitive project data held on behalf of government and critical-infrastructure clients, elevating national-security and export-control considerations for some firms.

id: student information systems sis and core records
name: Student Information Systems (SIS) and Core Records
description: The system of record for enrolment, demographics, attendance, discipline and transcripts, and the highest-value single target in education because it concentrates minors' PII for an entire district or institution in one platform. SIS compromise is both a direct exposure at the institution and, via the vendor, the sector's principal aggregation event - the PowerSchool intrusion reached a claimed 62.4 million students and 9.5 million teachers across approximately 6,505 districts.

id: learning management systems gradebooks and instructional platforms
name: Learning Management Systems, Gradebooks and Instructional Platforms
description: The day-to-day instructional layer - LMS, gradebook, courseware, assessment and proctoring tools. Outage halts teaching directly, and the platforms hold years of coursework, private messaging and behavioural data. The May 2026 Instructure/Canvas incident demonstrated the scale: attackers claimed 3.6TB covering 275 million users across roughly 9,000 institutions, including private student-teacher messages, in a platform used by 41% of US higher education institutions.

id: financial aid bursar payroll and payment systems
name: Financial Aid, Bursar, Payroll and Payment Systems
description: Education institutions process tuition, financial aid, donations, payroll and vendor payments, and financial-aid files in particular concentrate exactly the identity elements needed for fraud - SSNs, bank details and full household income data (FAFSA). Encryption here halts payroll and disbursement; exfiltration produces the sector's highest per-record identity-theft severity.

id: research data intellectual property and regulated research health data
name: Research Data, Intellectual Property and Regulated Research Health Data
description: The exposure unique to higher education. Universities hold pre-publication research, proprietary and licensed datasets, export-controlled work and long-running human-subjects cohorts. The University of Manchester attack reached NHS records for 1.1 million patients gathered from over 200 hospitals for medical research, and the University of Hawai'i Cancer Center incident exposed decades-old epidemiological cohort data affecting up to 1.15 million individuals - demonstrating that research archives create liability for populations who were never students or staff.

id: minors pii and sensitive student welfare records
name: Minors' PII and Sensitive Student Welfare Records
description: The sector's most reputationally and legally explosive exposure. Beyond routine PII, schools hold counselling notes, psychological evaluations, abuse and safeguarding reports, and custody arrangements for children who cannot consent and whose identities remain exploitable for decades. Both LAUSD and Minneapolis saw student psychological assessments published after refusing to pay, and Baltimore City Public Schools' 2025 incident exposed SSNs and driver's licence data for thousands of students and staff.

id: campus operational technology and physical safety systems
name: Campus Operational Technology and Physical Safety Systems
description: Schools and campuses run building and safety infrastructure on the same networks as administrative IT, so ransomware translates directly into physical-safety consequences and closure decisions. The Minneapolis breach was confirmed by analysts to have exposed school security blueprints - a worst-case outcome in which stolen data creates ongoing physical risk to children that no notification or credit monitoring can remediate.

id: alumni donor and advancement databases
name: Alumni, Donor and Advancement Databases
description: University advancement systems hold high-net-worth individuals' financial profiles, giving histories, wealth-screening assessments and private correspondence. This data is disproportionately valuable relative to its volume, and its exposure damages the institution's fundraising capacity - a material revenue line for higher education - well beyond the incident itself. The University of Manchester breach included alumni records alongside current student data.

id: third party edtech cloud and identity infrastructure
name: Third-Party Edtech, Cloud and Identity Infrastructure
description: Modern institutions outsource most of their data estate, so a large share of exposure sits outside the insured's own perimeter and outside its control. This is the exposure that converts individual education risks into portfolio-level correlated loss, and Verizon's 2026 DBIR reported third parties featuring in 48% of breaches with supply-chain breaches up 60% year over year.

id: operational technology and control systems
name: Operational Technology & Control Systems
description: The physical-process control estate unique to energy/utilities — the crown-jewel exposure whose compromise or precautionary shutdown halts energy delivery.

id: enterprise it and business critical applications
name: Enterprise IT & Business-Critical Applications
description: Corporate systems that, when encrypted, stop planning, dispatch, trading, and revenue — the layer most ransomware actually hits.

id: customer facing and retail systems
name: Customer-Facing & Retail Systems
description: Public-facing and downstream retail exposure, particularly acute for utilities and fuel-retail operators.

id: third parties and interconnections
name: Third Parties & Interconnections
description: External entities and links whose compromise transmits risk into or out of the operator.

id: core banking and payment systems
name: Core Banking and Payment Systems
description: The transactional backbone of financial institutions - direct targets or collateral damage in ransomware incidents that can halt money movement itself.

id: customer and counterparty data pii pfi
name: Customer and Counterparty Data (PII/PFI)
description: The high-value, highly regulated personal and financial data that makes this sector an attractive double-extortion target.

id: third party vendor and fintech partner ecosystem
name: Third-Party, Vendor, and Fintech-Partner Ecosystem
description: Financial institutions increasingly outsource operational functions and partner with fintechs, creating shared/concentrated exposure where a single vendor breach cascades across multiple unrelated institutions and their end customers.

id: market infrastructure and institutional systems
name: Market Infrastructure and Institutional Systems
description: Systems whose disruption has effects beyond the victim institution, spilling into broader market functioning - a distinguishing feature of ransomware exposure in this sector versus most others.

id: digital and remote access channels
name: Digital and Remote-Access Channels
description: Customer- and employee-facing digital surfaces that both enable ransomware entry and represent business-continuity exposure if taken offline.

id: corporate legal and governance records
name: Corporate, Legal, and Governance Records
description: Non-customer data whose exposure drives regulatory, legal, and reputational consequences distinct from direct financial fraud.

id: electronic health record ehr and clinical documentation systems
name: Electronic Health Record (EHR) and Clinical Documentation Systems
description: Core systems storing and managing patient charts, orders, and treatment history; encryption or unavailability directly halts clinical operations.

id: medical imaging lab and diagnostic systems
name: Medical Imaging, Lab, and Diagnostic Systems
description: Specialized clinical systems and connected devices whose disruption halts diagnosis and treatment pathways.

id: claims billing and revenue cycle infrastructure
name: Claims, Billing, and Revenue-Cycle Infrastructure
description: Financial and administrative processing systems, often centralized in a small number of national clearinghouses, that create systemic single points of failure.

id: telehealth and remote care platforms
name: Telehealth and Remote-Care Platforms
description: Patient-facing digital care delivery channels that expand the network's external attack surface.

id: protected health information phi and personal data
name: Protected Health Information (PHI) and Personal Data
description: The core data asset that makes healthcare an attractive double-extortion target, spanning highly sensitive clinical and identity data.

id: third party and vendor ecosystem
name: Third-Party and Vendor Ecosystem
description: The dense web of business associates and downstream partners that extend a healthcare organization's effective risk surface far beyond its own network.

id: physical operational continuity systems
name: Physical/Operational Continuity Systems
description: Facility and logistics systems whose disruption has direct patient-safety consequences distinct from pure data risk.

id: software development and source code assets
name: Software Development and Source-Code Assets
description: The crown-jewel assets unique to technology firms; their exposure enables both direct IP loss and downstream supply-chain compromise.

id: customer facing saas cloud platforms
name: Customer-Facing SaaS / Cloud Platforms
description: The revenue-generating production systems whose downtime directly halts thousands of customers.

id: managed services and remote management infrastructure
name: Managed-Services and Remote-Management Infrastructure
description: Tooling that grants privileged reach into customer estates, making it a high-value pivot for cascade attacks.

id: corporate it identity and edge systems
name: Corporate IT, Identity and Edge Systems
description: The internal backbone whose compromise enables lateral movement and encryption.

id: customer employee and third party data
name: Customer, Employee and Third-Party Data
description: IT firms hold vast volumes of both their own and their customers' data as processors, magnifying breach-notification and liability exposure.

id: distribution logistics and commerce systems
name: Distribution, Logistics and Commerce Systems
description: For IT distributors/resellers and platform providers, transactional systems are the business; their loss stops downstream commerce.

id: downstream ecosystem and supply chain relationships
name: Downstream Ecosystem and Supply-Chain Relationships
description: The third parties whose exposure flows through the IT firm, creating aggregation risk.

id: intellectual property and trade secrets
name: Intellectual property and trade secrets
description: Proprietary technical and strategic information distinct to scientific/technical consultancies.

id: operational technology industrial control systems ot ics scada
name: Operational Technology / Industrial Control Systems (OT/ICS/SCADA)
description: Physical production infrastructure that, unlike pure IT, ties ransomware impact directly to safety and physical output — the defining exposure that differentiates manufacturing from most other insured industries.

id: production and manufacturing execution systems
name: Production and Manufacturing Execution Systems
description: Software layers that plan, schedule, and track physical production — encryption or corruption here halts output even if OT hardware itself is untouched.

id: supply chain and third party vendor networks
name: Supply Chain and Third-Party/Vendor Networks
description: Manufacturing's deep tiered-supplier interdependency means exposure extends well beyond the insured entity's own network perimeter.

id: enterprise it and corporate data
name: Enterprise IT and Corporate Data
description: Conventional back-office systems that remain a primary initial-access and extortion target even in OT-heavy environments.

id: physical plant and multi site infrastructure
name: Physical Plant and Multi-Site Infrastructure
description: Geographically distributed physical facilities whose network segmentation (or lack thereof) determines how far a single compromise can spread.

id: client and case data
name: Client and case data
description: The core work-product and confidential records professional-services firms hold on behalf of clients.

id: crm sales and saas platforms
name: CRM, sales, and SaaS platforms
description: Cloud-hosted customer/contact systems increasingly targeted directly rather than via on-prem encryption.

id: erp back office and bpo processing systems
name: ERP, back-office, and BPO processing systems
description: Systems that process transactional and often highly regulated data on behalf of multiple end clients.

id: real estate specific systems and data
name: Real estate-specific systems and data
description: Systems and data unique to commercial/residential real estate services firms.

id: wholesale trade and logistics systems
name: Wholesale trade and logistics systems
description: Systems supporting the physical movement and distribution of goods.

id: employee contractor and third party data
name: Employee, contractor, and third-party data
description: Personal data of the firm's own workforce and its extended network of subcontractors/partners.

id: cloud msp infrastructure and credentials
name: Cloud/MSP infrastructure and credentials
description: The infrastructure and access pathways that, if compromised, enable one-to-many downstream compromise.

id: citizen and employee data assets
name: Citizen & Employee Data Assets
description: The sensitive personal and administrative records that make government a high-value data-extortion target.

id: core it and enterprise systems
name: Core IT & Enterprise Systems
description: The back-office and productivity systems whose encryption halts government operations.

id: citizen facing service platforms
name: Citizen-Facing Service Platforms
description: The public service-delivery systems whose downtime directly harms residents.

id: public safety and emergency systems
name: Public-Safety & Emergency Systems
description: Life-safety systems whose disruption elevates a data incident to a public-safety emergency.

id: operational technology and municipal infrastructure
name: Operational Technology & Municipal Infrastructure
description: Physical-world control systems owned or overseen by government bodies.

id: third party and shared service dependencies
name: Third-Party & Shared-Service Dependencies
description: External providers and shared platforms whose compromise exposes the agency (aggregation risk).

id: point of sale pos and payment systems
name: Point-of-Sale (POS) and Payment Systems
description: In-store POS terminals, payment gateways/processors, e-commerce checkout flows, and PCI-scoped cardholder data environments. Encryption or manipulation of these systems can halt in-store sales entirely; breach of stored/tokenized card data drives PCI-DSS liability.

id: customer data and crm loyalty platforms
name: Customer Data and CRM/Loyalty Platforms
description: Centralized repositories of customer PII, purchase history, and loyalty-program data, increasingly hosted in third-party SaaS/CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce) that have become a primary extortion target independent of on-prem encryption.

id: supply chain inventory and store operations systems
name: Supply Chain, Inventory, and Store Operations Systems
description: ERP, warehouse management, automated ordering, and inventory/replenishment systems whose disruption forces retailers back to manual, paper-based operations - the single biggest driver of revenue loss in major incidents like M&S.

id: third party franchise and vendor dealer networks
name: Third-Party, Franchise, and Vendor/Dealer Networks
description: Retail and consumer-services businesses depend heavily on shared platforms (DMS/SaaS providers), franchise networks, and outsourced IT help desks, creating single points of failure that can cascade an attack on one vendor into thousands of affected businesses.

id: employee and hr data
name: Employee and HR Data
description: Large, often lower-wage, high-turnover workforces mean retailers and consumer-services firms hold extensive employee PII, frequently a secondary but highly damaging data-theft target.

id: physical and building adjacent operational technology
name: Physical and Building-Adjacent Operational Technology
description: Consumer-services subsectors (grocery, hospitality, fitness, healthcare-adjacent services) operate physical/IoT systems whose disruption creates safety and spoilage risk beyond pure data loss.

id: brand product and intellectual property data
name: Brand, Product, and Intellectual Property Data
description: Unreleased product designs, pricing strategy, and brand assets are targeted for extortion leverage distinct from customer-data theft, particularly in fashion/apparel and consumer product goods.

id: core network and signaling systems
name: Core Network & Signaling Systems
description: The 'OT-equivalent' layer for telecom - subscriber and routing infrastructure whose compromise or outage disrupts service for large customer populations rather than just exposing records.

id: subscriber and customer pii
name: Subscriber & Customer PII
description: The high-volume personal data telecom operators uniquely hold by virtue of serving as national-scale identity and communications intermediaries.

id: enterprise backend it and saas platforms
name: Enterprise/Backend IT & SaaS Platforms
description: The corporate IT layer - often the actual initial-access and lateral-movement surface even when the attacker's goal is subscriber or infrastructure data.

id: physical and field infrastructure
name: Physical & Field Infrastructure
description: Telecom's unusual exposure of physical assets and access controls alongside digital ones - a hazard largely absent in pure IT/software industries.

id: third party partner and downstream data
name: Third-Party, Partner & Downstream Data
description: Data and access that telecom operators hold on behalf of, or shared with, other organizations - amplifying blast radius beyond the operator's own customers.

id: regulatory lawful intercept and critical infrastructure systems
name: Regulatory, Lawful-Intercept & Critical-Infrastructure Systems
description: Government-facing and critical-infrastructure-designated systems that create outsized regulatory and national-security exposure when compromised.

id: fleet freight and operational technology systems
name: Fleet, Freight & Operational Technology Systems
description: The operational core of transportation/warehousing firms — systems whose downtime directly halts the physical movement of goods, distinguishing this industry's ransomware exposure from purely data-centric sectors.

id: customer shipment and financial data
name: Customer, Shipment & Financial Data
description: Sensitive business and transactional data whose exposure drives breach-notification duties and extortion leverage even when operations aren't disrupted.

id: physical and critical infrastructure assets
name: Physical & Critical-Infrastructure Assets
description: Because transportation is designated critical infrastructure in most jurisdictions, exposure extends beyond data to physical assets and public safety/regulatory systems.
